module_title: Types of Ownership & Possession, and Hohfeld's Basic Matrix
introduction: This intermediate tier drives into the classification of Ownership and Possession. It also introduces the first half of Wesley Newcomb Hohfeld's legendary framework, which mathematically organizes how legal words like 'Right', 'Duty', and 'Liberty' interact.

core_concepts.title: Types of Ownership
core_concepts.description:
1. Corporeal vs. Incorporeal: Corporeal is ownership of physical things (land, car). Incorporeal is ownership of intangible rights (patents, copyrights, trademarks).
2. Sole vs. Co-ownership: Sole is owned by one person. Co-ownership is shared by two or more (e.g., joint tenants).
3. Trust vs. Beneficial: A Trustee owns the property strictly for the benefit of another. The Beneficiary has the actual enjoyment/beneficial ownership.
4. Vested vs. Contingent: Vested ownership is perfect and immediate. Contingent ownership depends on the fulfillment of an uncertain future condition.

core_concepts.title: Types of Possession
core_concepts.description:
1. Immediate vs. Mediate: Immediate (Direct) is when you hold the object yourself. Mediate (Indirect) is when you possess it through an agent or servant (e.g., you own a car, but your driver is driving it; you have mediate possession).
2. Constructive Possession: Possession in law, without actual physical possession. (e.g., A seller hands over the keys of a warehouse to the buyer. Handing over the keys transfers 'constructive possession' of the goods inside).

core_concepts.title: Hohfeld's Jural Analysis: The Basics
core_concepts.description:
Hohfeld argued that lawyers use the word 'Right' too loosely. He broke it down into 8 distinct concepts, arranged in Correlatives (things that exist together) and Opposites (things that cannot coexist).

First Matrix (First-Order Rights):
- Jural Correlatives (If A has X, B must have Y):
  * RIGHT <---> DUTY (If I have a *Right* to my car, you have a *Duty* not to touch it).
  * PRIVILEGE (Liberty) <---> NO-RIGHT (If I have the *Privilege* to wear a green shirt, you have *No-Right* to stop me).

core_concepts.title: Hohfeld's Jural Opposites
core_concepts.description:
Jural Opposites (If A has X, A cannot have Y):
* RIGHT <---> NO-RIGHT (You cannot have a right and a no-right over the same thing).
* DUTY <---> PRIVILEGE/LIBERTY (If you have a duty to do something, you do not have the privilege/liberty to not do it).

important_entities.name: Res Nullius
important_entities.key_fact: A thing belonging to no one.
important_entities.significance: How is possession originally acquired? By taking control of *Res Nullius* (e.g., catching a wild fish in the ocean). The first person to establish Corpus and Animus over a previously unowned thing acquires original possession.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a thief steals your watch, does the thief have possession? **YES**. The thief has physical control (Corpus) and the intent to keep it (Animus). Does the thief have ownership? **NO**. Possession is a matter of fact; ownership is a matter of law. The law will protect the thief's possession against a second thief, but not against you (the true owner).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Always pair these together. They are two sides of the exact same coin. A's Right is B's Duty.

exam_strategy_tips: In CLAT PG or UGC NET, 'Match the Following' questions based on Hohfeld's Correlatives and Opposites are almost guaranteed. Memorize the exact pairings: Right correlates to Duty. Privilege correlates to No-Right.
